occupation: Software Engineer, Computer Programmer, Open Source Developer
school: Operating Systems, Computer Security, Open Source Software
legacy: Theo de Raadt became one of the most influential figures in secure open-source software development. Through his leadership and technical direction, he helped establish a culture that prioritizes correctness, transparency and security in operating system design.
earlyLife: Growing up with an interest in computing and software, de Raadt was drawn to the technical challenges of operating systems and low-level programming. His fascination with system reliability and code quality eventually led him to participate in major open-source projects and later create his own.
scientificField: Software Engineering, Computer Security, Operating Systems
majorContributions: De Raadt is best known for founding OpenBSD, a project focused on security, careful code review and reliability. Under his guidance, the project produced technologies that became widely used throughout the computing industry. His emphasis on proactive security practices influenced how many developers approach software engineering and infrastructure protection.
laterLife: As OpenBSD matured, de Raadt continued directing development efforts while encouraging rigorous coding standards and detailed security reviews. His work helped maintain one of the most respected security-focused software projects in the open-source community.
whyImportant: Many security technologies used across servers, networks and internet infrastructure emerged from projects associated with Theo de Raadt. His focus on secure-by-default systems demonstrated that careful engineering can significantly improve software trustworthiness.
